subject: Renewal: SentryTech reserved-pool scale and token-band SLOs
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@sentrytech.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>
Cc: SentryTech Procurement <procurement@sentrytech.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning: adding reserved GPUs + throughput SLA

Hi Elliot,

We're preparing our Q2 renewal and want to expand our dedicated capacity with Redwood. Over the past 6 months our burst needs have grown; we're proposing to add 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs to our existing reserved pool (for a total of 24 GPUs) and to formalize a tokens/sec guarantee for the pool during business hours (US PST 8am-6pm).

Specifically SentryTech would like:
- A committed reserved pool of 24 GPUs (8 additional)
- A minimum steady-state throughput guarantee of 3,200 tokens/sec across the pool for production traffic (with detailed token accounting included in the addendum)
- Clear SLOs and penalties or credits if throughput underperforms on monthly rolling windows

Can you share a proposed addendum and the estimated delta to our renewal price? We need this for our procurement cycle — can you get a draft by next Monday?

Attachments: current_usage_report.csv (referenced)

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Sr. ML Platform Lead
SentryTech

From: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@sentrytech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Feb 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: adding reserved GPUs + throughput SLA

Hi Laura — great to hear the usage growth, congrats on the momentum.

We can absolutely structure an addendum for the reserved pool expansion and a tokens/sec SLO. Initial thoughts:
- Add 8 GPUs to the reserved pool effective at renewal start date; we can offer a ramp window for burst budget during first 30 days.
- Throughput guarantee: we propose defining the SLO as "sustained tokens/sec over 10-minute aggregation windows during business hours" and a monthly service credit if sustained shortfall exceeds 4 hours per month.
- Fallback: automatic model-variant routing (lower-cost quantized variant) for non-critical workloads to preserve production SLOs.

I'll get a draft addendum (redline and plain text) over to you by Monday EOD. For budgeting: rough delta is +$56k/month for the 8 GPUs + a small surcharge for the contractual SLO/penalty coverage — I'll confirm exact figures with finance and loop Marissa.

I'll attach a working draft and a simple workbook showing token accounting. Can we do a short call tomorrow 10am PST to confirm acceptance criteria?

Best,
Elliot Price
Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0124

Attachment: (will send) reserved-pool-throughput-addendum-draft.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Feb 2027 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Renewal planning: adding reserved GPUs + throughput SLA

Elliot — looping finance and solutions. A few constraints from pricing:
- We can price the 8 GPUs as committed capacity at a 12-month term with a 6% discount versus a month-to-month uplift.
- Service credit levels: proposal below (subject to legal review):
  * Tier 1: <= 4 hours monthly shortfall = 0% credit
  * Tier 2: >4 and <=12 hours = 5% monthly credit on committed capacity portion
  * Tier 3: >12 hours = 12% monthly credit
- Need to define how tokens are measured (ingested vs. generated), whether system-level throttling counts as shortfall, and how multi-tenant burst activity factors into pool calculations.

Aditya — can you validate the rough delta Elliot mentioned and produce the renewal quote? Neha — can you draft a crisp SLO paragraph we can include in the addendum (one-paragraph legal-friendly wording + a short appendix for measurement)?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Director, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Renewal planning: adding reserved GPUs + throughput SLA

Marissa / team — draft SLO language below (keeps measurement simple and defensible):

SLO (Reserved-Pool Throughput):
"Redwood will provide a committed reserved GPU pool consisting of 24 GPUs for the Customer. During business hours (08:00-18:00 PST, Monday-Friday excluding Redwood-observed holidays), Redwood guarantees a minimum sustained throughput of 3,200 tokens/sec measured at the API ingress aggregated across all instances in the reserved pool using 10-minute sampling windows. A sustained shortfall is recorded when the 10-minute sampled throughput is below the guaranteed level. Monthly service credits will accrue as follows: Tier A — no credits for cumulative shortfall <= 4 hours; Tier B — 5% credit of the monthly committed capacity fee for cumulative shortfall >4 and <=12 hours; Tier C — 12% credit for cumulative shortfall >12 hours. Credits exclude overage and burst billing. Redwood's obligations under this SLO do not apply to outages caused by Customer configuration, third-party cloud provider failures, or force majeure events."

Appendix (measurement):
- Metric: API-inserted tokens/sec as recorded by the Redwood control plane metric (metric id: redwood.reserved_pool.tokens_per_sec).
- Aggregation: 10-minute rolling windows, converted to hours for monthly tally.
- Dispute window: Customer must raise measurement disputes within 15 calendar days of the monthly report.

I'm attaching a redline doc with these clauses and a short sample calculation spreadsheet. Suggest we keep penalties as credits only (no cash refunds) to reduce legal friction.

Attachments: reserved-pool-throughput-addendum-draft.docx

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
